changes.how: In storeHosts() (lines 35 to 42) keep the last parse. Add two module variables above it: `let parsedFrom: string | null = null; let parsedHosts: StoreHosts = {};`. The body becomes: `const raw = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_HOSTS || "{}"; if (raw === parsedFrom) return parsedHosts;` then the existing try/catch parse into a local `next` ({} on a failure or a non-object), then deep-freeze it (Object.freeze the map, each store's entry, its `hosts` array and its `languages` and `countries` objects when present), then `parsedFrom = raw; parsedHosts = next; return next;`. The memory is keyed on the text, never on first use: tests stub the variable between cases and must see the new value. Update the doc comment: parsed once per instance and frozen, because it is now shared.

Add a case 'the hosts list is parsed once': build a 1,000-store list (`Object.fromEntries(Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, i) => [`s${i}`, { primary: `shop${i}.example.no`, hosts: [`shop${i}.example.no`] }]))`), stub NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_DOMAIN to 'kaizenstore.site' and NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_HOSTS to its JSON with vi.stubEnv, then `const spy = vi.spyOn(JSON, 'parse');` call `marketPath('s1', 'no', '/cart')` 1,000 times, expect `spy.mock.calls.length` to be at most 1, restore the spy. Then stub NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_HOSTS to another text (one store with another primary) and expect storeOrigin() of that store to give the new primary (a changed text is seen by the next call). End with vi.unstubAllEnvs() as the file's other cases do.
